🛑 Requirement: Exercise the debug-only tests in CI

This build constraint excludes the override and invalid-input tests from the existing CI invocation, which uses only the integration tag (.github/workflows/go.yml:32). The build step also omits ghdebug, so this workflow does not compile or test the enabled implementation. Add a separate ghdebug-tagged test invocation covering internal/debug and the factory override tests, while retaining the regular run to cover the disabled implementation.

Not changing this one. The `ghdebug` build is a developer tool for testing token expiry, used rarely, and it never ships. Running a second tagged test pass on every OS in the matrix is more CI cost than it is worth for that. The production side is already covered by the regular run: release builds compile `config_disabled.go`, and `TestConfigIgnoresEnvironment` asserts that `Config()` returns no overrides even when the `GH_INTERNAL_*` variables are set. If the enabled implementation breaks, it shows up as soon as someone runs `make debug` or the e2e scripts, which only affects whoever is building the debug binary.

🛑 Requirement: Test the verbose-refresh override through the HTTP client

TestTokenRefresherHttpClient only checks default headline-only logging. The new debug-package tests check parsing, so they would still pass if this assignment were reversed or the override were ignored. Add ghdebug-enabled client tests with GH_DEBUG=api: true should include verbose request/response lines, while explicit false should retain headline-only logging. Reuse the existing local HTTP test setup and isolate the override environment variables.

Not changing this one either. Without the CI step from the other thread, a `ghdebug` tagged test here would only run when someone opts in, so it would mostly go stale. What matters for users is that release builds never log a verbose refresh trace, and that is already guarded: in a regular build `VerboseTokenRefresh` is always `None`, so `logHeadlineOnly` keeps its default of `true`, and `TestTokenRefresherHttpClient` asserts that `GH_DEBUG=api` logs only the head line with no `> POST` or `< HTTP` lines. The override itself only affects debug builds, where a regression would be obvious to whoever turned it on.

**Change Requested**

A plain `make` needs to restore an untagged binary after `make debug`. It currently leaves `bin/gh` as a debug build because `script/build` considers the existing binary current.

```console
$ make debug >/dev/null
$ bin/gh version | head -n 1
gh version 2.100.0-183-gfbc22f97c (2026-10-19) [debug build]
$ make
build.go: `bin/gh` is up to date.
$ bin/gh version | head -n 1
gh version 2.100.0-183-gfbc22f97c (2026-10-19) [debug build]
```

I think the debug build needs a separate output path, or the build needs to account for tags.

 	@script/build$(EXE) $@
 
+# Builds bin/gh with the ghdebug build tag, which enables the GH_INTERNAL_* overrides in internal/debug.
+# The existing binary is removed first because script/build skips rebuilding when sources are unchanged.
+.PHONY: debug
+debug: script/build$(EXE)
+	@rm -f bin/gh$(EXE)
+	@GO_BUILDTAGS=ghdebug script/build$(EXE) bin/gh$(EXE)

nodes.body: Good catch, thanks! Fixed in 3acdfcdcb. `script/build` now reads the build tags recorded in the existing `bin/gh` and compares them with `GO_BUILDTAGS`, so it rebuilds whenever they differ. A plain `make` after `make debug` now produces a regular build again (and the same goes for any `make GO_BUILDTAGS=...`). Repeating the same build still skips an up to date binary, and `make debug` no longer needs to delete `bin/gh` first.

**Suggestion**

Non blocking, and I feel 3/10 strongly about this. Could we run the `ghdebug` variant in CI so the tagged implementation cannot silently stop compiling?

```console
$ git show origin/pr-14752:.github/workflows/go.yml | grep 'go test'
        run: go test -race -tags=integration ./...
```

The regular run should stay so we also cover the disabled implementation. What do you think?

Good point, thanks! :pray: I took a slightly different route that makes a tagged test run unnecessary.

In 8f43becdf I moved the environment parsing out of `config_enabled.go` into an unexported `configFromEnv` in the untagged `config.go`. That way `config_test.go` covers every parsing and panic case in the regular test run, on every OS. What is left behind the tag is just the choice of what `Config` returns:

- `ghdebug`: `return configFromEnv()`
- `!ghdebug`: `return DebugConfig{}`, which `TestConfigIgnoresEnvironment` already asserts in the regular run

Since the release `Config` never references `configFromEnv`, the linker drops it from regular builds. I checked the resulting binaries for linux/amd64, windows/amd64, windows/arm64, darwin/amd64, and darwin/arm64: every regular build has no `GH_INTERNAL_` strings and no parser symbols at all (only the `Config` stub), while every `ghdebug` build has all three variable names along with `configFromEnv` and `lifetimeFromEnv`.

So the only way the debug variant can break without the regular run noticing is by failing to compile, and d5d4d81bb covers that with a `go build -tags=ghdebug ./cmd/gh` step on the Ubuntu runner. Running the whole suite again with the tag would buy us nothing extra, and since Go caches test results per tag set it would rerun every package on every OS.

**Suggestion**

Non blocking, and I feel 3/10 strongly about this. The new tests cover parsing, but not whether this client or the expiry consumers apply each option correctly.

```console
$ git grep -l -E 'GH_INTERNAL_(AT_EXPIRES_IN|RT_EXPIRES_IN|DEBUG_REFRESH_TOKEN)' origin/pr-14752 -- '*_test.go'
origin/pr-14752:internal/debug/config_disabled_test.go
origin/pr-14752:internal/debug/config_enabled_test.go
```

Could we add tagged tests for logging `true` and `false`, plus access and refresh token expiry? What do you think?

Thanks! Same reasoning as my reply to Copilot here: these paths only matter in debug builds, and the release default (headline only logging) is already covered by `TestTokenRefresherHttpClient`. I'll leave the tagged tests out for now.

### 🟡 Changes recommended Debug-only behavior needs HTTP-client logging regression tests and a tagged CI test invocation.
